pr_title: Fix some errors reported by Coverity
pr_body:
##### Summary
Fixes #6791 

This PR fixes the following errors found in the report delivered by Coverity on 09/05/2019:

CID 348627: Considering that the official documentation fdopen(3) says "The file descriptor is not dup'ed, and will be closed when the stream created by fdopen() is  closed.", I choice to use `fclose` instead `close()` and `fp =NULL`.
CID 348628: There was a real possibility to clean a structure and use it after this, so I introducted a test for the pointer.
CID 348629: It was changed the call from stat for a file pointer movement to measure the file size.
CID 348635: It was added a conditional to verify the existence of the address before to test the first value of a pointer.
CID 348638: Without any doubt our current code is the safest option, so I did not touch it.
CID 348639: We have a reuse of pointer here that generates this wrong error message.
CID 348640: We do not have resource leak here, because in this case Netdata always given an allocated structure
CID 348641: I added an if to verify the return, and I am calling perror to redirect the data to error.log.
CID 348643: The function here is never used inside Netdata, so I removed it.
CID 348646: Clion is saying that Cups plugin is not linked, and here I confess I agree with the error reported, but I do not know the whole structure, so I am for others to do an study about this case.

I did not touch the code related with dbengine due talk in Slack channel.
##### Component Name
Netdata core
##### Additional Information
pr_comments: @thiagoftsm many thanks for the PR. As a note, however, you should have split your work with clean commits, one per Coverity issue.

> @thiagoftsm many thanks for the PR. As a note, however, you should have split your work with clean commits, one per Coverity issue.

You are welcome @cosmix! I created only one, because there was only one report, and I imagined that would be simple to do the association between errors and fixes here, but I agree with you that it would be more clean to have the fixes per issue, but we have sometimes more  than one bug in specific files. Can we at least to do PRs per file? Remeber we are talking about 23 bugs.
No I meant one commit per Coverity issue. Not one PR per Coverity issue :)
@mfundul I removed the `if` and `error()` from libnetdata/popen/popen.c when we call the `fcntl` and I decided to use `(void)`, because we were generating thousands of error message.

Manage this branch in Squash

Test this branch here: https://coverity-20190905-908yn.squash.io

issue_context.title: Coverity Scan Defects 5/9/19

review_comments: I used the same solution that I used above, now I will check an error that we are having with custom_peopen.
If you do `ps = NULL;` it will crash immediately afterwards in line 252: `ssize_t r = read(ps->capacity->fd, buffer, 30);`

Actually, I don't get that `read` at all. Even in the previous version, we should end up segfaulting when `ps->capacity->fd == -1`, right? I mean, it zeroes everything. Looks like the code is missing an `} else {` here.
It probably did not segfault immediately due to it not being NULL. We either need to move the code in the `if (ps)` or use an `else` as you suggested.
I decided to use an `else`, I tested both to see what would be more readable, and I confess I liked more the `else`.
This does not break cleanly out of the 2 nested loops and it can be called multiple times in theory. That would be `free()` after `free()` which sounds bad.

But still the code can go to `pr = pr->next` from:
```
for(pr = ps->property_root; pr && !read_error; pr = pr->next) {
```
and call `power_supply_free(ps);` again?
The `read_error` variable avoid it continues going in the next element of the for loop, as you can see it is set to `1`, every time we clean the structure.
Then I guess `ps = NULL;` is not really necessary because the next use is only `struct power_supply *ps = power_supply_root;` ?
I agree 100%, I removed the unnecessary set of a variable. Thank you!
So what should happen in this case? What should we do if `silencers_filename` is empty? Nothing?

The silencers_filename is not a file that always exists, it only exists case the user talks with the Agent and  send a message to it stores the health information inside this file. When this file does not exists, the Agent works with its default behavior.
